report.summary: All three failures come from one product bug: `book_dict` in app/main.py:144 returns the year under the key `published`, while the POST response, the PUT response, and the books.html template all use `year`. Fix this first, by making `book_dict` return `year` (or updating every consumer to `published`, but `year` matches the rest of the app and the tests). The fix should clear all three failures with no test changes.

causes.title: GET /api/books/{id}, the book list, and the UI report the year under `published` instead of `year`
causes.explanation: book_dict() renames the year column to `published`. Create (insert_book) and update (api_update_book) return the BookIn model dump, which uses `year`. So a created or updated book has a different shape when read back. Both API tests compare the GET body against the create/update body and fail on exactly this key. The UI also uses list_books() through book_dict, and books.html:19 renders `b.year`. That key does not exist in the dict, so Jinja renders it empty, and the year cell is blank. This is deterministic, not timing-related. The app's own API is inconsistent, so the test expectations are reasonable and the application is wrong.
evidence: app/main.py:160: insert_book returns `{"id": cur.lastrowid, **book.model_dump()}`, which has `year`
app/main.py:218: api_update_book returns `{"id": book_id, **book.model_dump()}`, which has `year`
app/templates/books.html:19: `{{ b.year or "" }}`, which reads a key that book_dict never sets
tests/api/test_books_api.py:17: `assert fetched.json() == book` fails with 'Left contains 1 more item: {'published': 1965}' vs 'Right contains 1 more item: {'year': 1965}'
tests/api/test_books_api.py:26-28: expects GET to return `"year": 2001`; actual is `published: 2001`
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:16: `expect(books.row(title)).to_contain_text("1965")` fails; the actual row text is 'Dune-a4f89e68 / Frank Herbert / Delete' with no year
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py book_dict(), change the key `published` to `year` so reads match create/update responses and the template. Then check that nothing else depends on `published` (grep the repo, including the frontend and any API clients). Rerun the three tests.
